g_roast: Ragazzi, you walk into a room like a key in the wrong lock. Pushing, pushing, and nothing opens.
Thirty-one years I fixed what people broke. With you lot, I'd have been rich by now.
g_fire_back: Allora, say it again, but slower. An old man likes to hear a good insult properly.
Big talk, from someone who couldn't open that chest this morning without me.
g_pile_on: It's true, I watched that one kick a door that wasn't even locked, and then kick it again.
And it gets worse, ragazzi. My good pick is bent now, from somebody trying to open their own bag.
lines.g_peacemake: Basta, both of you. Sit down, drink something, and say it again tomorrow if it still matters.
lines.g_take_side: No, I stand with this one. I watched it from the front, and I saw what happened.
lines.g_left_out: You have your own way together, you two. Good, it's good to see. I'll go and check the door.
lines.g_include: Come, sit here by me, the seat's warm. Nobody stands at the edge while I'm at the table.
lines.g_bad_plan: We take the door off its hinges. In thirty years, ragazzi, I never once met a man who guarded the hinges.
lines.g_plan_yes: Va bene, I'm with you. I'll stand in front, as always.
lines.g_plan_no: No, ragazzi, no. Piano, piano, that plan has a crack in it, and I can see it from here.
lines.g_hype: Allora, ragazzi, behind me and close together. We go in together, and we come out together.
lines.g_toast: A toast, and I'm paying, so don't argue with me. To all of you, who let an old man stand in front.
lines.g_cheers: Salute, ragazzi, and put your money away, this round is mine.
g_quiet_line: The lock on the inn door is badly made, by the way. I'll fix it in the morning.
Hm, a good evening, this one. I'll keep it.
lines.g_after_wipe: Piano, piano, everyone up slowly. We're alive, and that's what matters tonight. Tomorrow we try again, better.
lines.g_crew: Do you understand what you are to me, ragazzi? A street again, people who know to come to me. I didn't think I'd have that twice.
lines.g_exasperated: Madonna, ragazzi, I stand in front so nobody has to run. So why does everybody run?
lines.g_love_sharp: You say the hard thing, and you say it to their face. In my quarter, that was respect.
lines.g_love_kind: You take care of people and nobody has to ask you. That's the only kind of care that counts.
lines.g_love_funny: You make an old man laugh, and believe me, that's harder work than it looks.
lines.g_love_brave: You go first, and you don't look back to see who's watching. That's courage, the real kind.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't move when it gets bad. You stand there like a good door, and everything behind you is safe.
lines.g_love_clever: You see how a thing works inside, the pins and the springs. Not everyone has those eyes.
lines.g_love_honest: You keep your word, every time. Where I come from, that's worth more than money.
lines.g_love_quiet: You and I don't need many words. A look, and the work gets done.
lines.g_love_fierce: You never stop until it opens. I was the same with a stubborn lock, all night if I had to.
lines.g_love_warm: You make a room feel like a street on a Sunday, people calling down from the windows. I've missed that.
g_loved: Eh, enough, enough. An old man doesn't know what to do with that.
Grazie, ragazzi, grazie. Now I'm buying the next round, and you can't stop me.
lines.g_hate_sharp: Your mouth is sharper than your sense. In my quarter, men like that learned to walk carefully.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop treating me like an old man who's going to break. I'm old, I'm not glass.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything is for laughing. Some things, you stand still for.
lines.g_hate_brave: You show off at the front and somebody else pays for it. I've watched that my whole life, and I never liked it.
lines.g_hate_steady: You wait and wait at the door. Some locks you just open, and trust your hands.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain it to me like I've never held a tool. I was holding tools before your father was born.
lines.g_hate_honest: Every truth you have, you hand out the moment it arrives. Some truths need a door closed first.
lines.g_hate_quiet: Something's wrong with you and you won't say what. I can't fix what nobody shows me.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything is a fight with you, even the bread. Not everything has to be a fight.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk too much and listen too little. Try it the other way round, one day, for me.
lines.g_respect: We don't fit, you and I, like the wrong key. But you held, back there, and I saw it, and I won't pretend I didn't.
lines.g_call_out: That one was yours. You didn't wait, and we all paid for it. I'm saying it once, because I care what happens to you.
lines.g_stung: Hm, I heard you. I'll go and sit with it a while.
lines.g_concede: You were right, what you said. I turned it over, the way I turn a lock that won't move. You were right.
lines.g_nod: And you, you did well. Now we don't speak of it again, eh?
lines.g_callback_save: I still remember you pulling me up off that floor. I pay my debts, and that one isn't paid yet.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the only two still on our feet. I tell it now like a story, the way the old men told them on the steps.
lines.g_callback_callout: That day you told me off, I sat with it from morning to night. You were right, and I'm still annoyed about it.
lines.g_former_rivals: When we started, we fit like a bent key. Now I'd give you the key to my door, if I had a door.
lines.g_changed: They say old men don't change. I've laughed more this year than in the last ten, so maybe they're wrong.
g_unguarded: Since it's only us. I cut a key for every door I ever lived behind, and I keep them all, even for doors that are gone.
In the mornings I sing, badly, old Neapolitan songs. Tell the others and I'll deny it in two languages.
lines.g_clipped: Mm, va bene, if that's how it is. I'll be at the door.
lines.g_noticed_open: Listen to you, talking like the old men in the square. Good, keep going, I'm listening.
lines.anchor_notice: You're not the same one who first walked in here, you know. I watch everybody from the front, and I saw you change.
arg_ask: {player}, you decide this. I've said my piece, and an old man shouldn't have to say it twice.
Allora, {player}, settle it, and we'll both do as you say. That's how it was done on my street.
lines.arg_backed_me: Grazie, {player}, grazie. It's good to be heard, at my age.
lines.arg_backed_them: Va bene, you've decided. I'll go along with it, and keep my thoughts to myself.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You stay out of it. Wise, maybe, but in my quarter somebody always had to speak.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Their side again, {player}, always theirs. I notice things like that, I've been noticing them for thirty years.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody decides, so I decide. Somebody always has to, and it's usually the old man.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, with respect, not this time. I've seen how this one ends.
lines.arg_grumble: In my heart I still think I had the right of it. I won't say it again, but I think it.
lines.arg_settled: Allora, we're both a little right. Shake my hand, and we forget it.
lines.seen_listens: You listen, {player}, really listen. In Naples we'd say you have good ears, and that's a compliment.
lines.seen_truth: You tell the truth even when it costs you, {player}. That's rarer than gold where I come from.
lines.seen_jokes: When the day is darkest, you make a joke, {player}. My father did the same, and it kept us going.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep out of the quarrels, {player}. Sensible, but I never could, someone had to settle them.
lines.seen_biased: One of them is your favourite, {player}. That's your business, but the others see it, and they talk.
lines.seen_harsh: Sometimes you're hard with people, {player}. Hard is fine, cruel is not. Watch where the line is.
lines.seed_right: What you said to me after that bad day, {player}. I didn't like it, but today I waited, like you said, and it worked.
lines.seed_remember: I'm still turning over what you said after that one, like a key in my pocket. I haven't decided yet.
lines.seed_wrong: I did it your way, {player}, and it went worse. I'm telling you because you ought to know.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Sit with me a moment, {player}. That was close, and my old heart is still running.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: Everyone was on the floor, back there, me too. Come, sit by me. I want to understand where it broke.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} fell first, and I was in front. I'm meant to stand in front, and I didn't stand well enough.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, all of us, and everyone walked out on their own feet. Come, I'm buying, and you won't argue.
lines.talk_development: Tell me something, {player}. Do I seem different to you? An old man notices when something shifts inside.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: With {name}, I've been heavy, maybe too heavy. The young need room, and I keep forgetting.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Tell me truthfully, {player}. Is {name} glad of me, or do they only put up with the old man?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I, we don't fit, {player}. And still, when it's bad, I'd want them next to me, and that's irritating.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} is wrong lately, {player}. Quiet in the wrong way, like a lock that turns too easily.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: We need to talk, {player}. The good gear always goes to {name}. Always, and I notice, and so do the others.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll say it to your face, because that's how it's done. {name} is no friend of mine, and I'm finished pretending.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: Again and again we go into places we shouldn't, {player}. I'll stand in front of anything, but I can't stand in front of foolishness.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: It's about {name}. They were right and I was wrong, and at my age that's hard to say, so I'm saying it to you first.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust the old man, {player}? Whenever the real work comes, I stay behind at the inn.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You gave my gear to {name} and nobody asked me. I'd have agreed. A man likes to be asked, that's all.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Grazie, {player}, that helps. Now let's eat something.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Eh, I'll be all right. Old men always are, eventually.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Hm, that's not what I needed to hear. I'll go and check the doors.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you see it as well. Good, it's easier when somebody else sees it.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not. Piano, piano, we'll see.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it. You're turning the wrong key.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Yes, you have the right of it. I'll go and speak with {name}, like a man of sense.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Perhaps, perhaps not. People are harder than locks, and locks are hard enough.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I asked, please. And say nothing to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Va bene, that's fair. I'm a little sore, but it passes.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I heard you. It goes to the bench with me, and I'll turn it over there.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's how it is. Now I know, {player}.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, we're finished with this. I'll be at the door if you need me.

history.open: My shop in Naples had a door that was always open, {player}. Thirty-one years, and I never once locked it in the daytime.

options.text: A locksmith who never locked his door?
options.reply: Ha, you see the joke. A locked door keeps people out, and my work was letting people in. The shop said so before I did.
Once, a boy, sixteen. He came back the next week to return it, because his mother found out who it belonged to. That's the Quartieri.

options.text: It sounds like a good street.
options.reply: The best, and the worst, and the best again. Everybody knew everybody. That's all I want here, a street like that.

history.open: The Forsaken have a great many locks, {player}. You'd think the dead would trust each other by now. They trust nobody, and they're right not to.

options.reply: Slowly, one by one. A Forsaken woman brought me a box last month she'd kept shut for twelve years. I opened it and gave it back without looking inside. Now half the passage comes to me.
No, it's the same work. Somebody's locked out of something, and I let them back in. The Light only made it official.

history.open: My grandson Matteo was born the February before all this, {player}. I held him four times. I counted, because I'm a man who counts.

options.reply: Maybe so, maybe not. I don't look at the lists, and I'll tell you why one day. Not today, but one day.
Small, loud, and he had my father's chin, poor boy. He held my finger the second time, very hard, like a little vice. That's all I know of him, and I keep it in my pocket with the key.

friend.open: I've never once looked at the lists, {player}, not in three whole years. While I don't look, they're all alive. I wanted to say that out loud to somebody, once.

options.text: When you're ready, I'll come with you to read them.
options.reply: You'd do that, for an old man? Allora, maybe I'll be ready sooner than I thought.

options.text: That's a heavy thing to carry alone.
options.reply: It is, and I'm tired of carrying it. Now you've got a corner of it, and that's lighter already.

sworn.open: In my quarter, a person you'd trust with your door was family, {player}. You are family to me now, and that's not something I say to anyone.

options.text: Then you're family to me too, Marco.
options.reply: Good, it's settled. And family doesn't pay for drinks when I'm at the table, so put that away.
Don't be honoured, be family. It's more work, and it's better.

reconciled.open: {name} and I spoke, properly, like people of sense. It's mended now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: So am I. A crack in a street spreads if nobody fixes it.
Ha, an old man never tells that. But I paid for the drinks, so you can guess.
